criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The world is real and bold. It has a near-black sky, a lit bunk lip and a gold windrow on 1, and a raked pool on caliche with stakes and pebble contact on 5, which is the STAGE done right. More than one frame falls to the 7 descriptor's single exception, though. Slide 8 is a close crop on a primitive kit steer: the hide texture is smeared, the back contour is doubled at about y 680 to 760, the ear flap cuts through the horn, and it fails the zoom test at full size. Slide 9's figure is a stiff A-pose mannequin, and the pipe post rises straight out of her cap. On slide 2 the four-section bunk is a thin band from y 1080 to 1340, about an eighth of the frame height, in a void. Slide 4 has no subject that owns the frame: the steers are about 40 px tall, the lamp pools are brown smudges, and both labels sit on dark plates. Slide 7 is a page on a flat mauve mid-tone backdrop with no true black, the quote's type is axis-aligned while the sheet is skewed, and machine QA warns of a dead lower zone. The steers on 1 and 6 have lilac legs from the fill light.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One feedyard at last light runs through all nine frames. The key comes from the west on every rendered frame, and the precast bunk changes state as a real motif: full on 1, sectioned as money on 2, one unset section on 5, a line of steers on 6, a rail on 7 and 8, and fed and empty on 9. The value track stays dark (art preflight medians: L* 5.6, 2.8 and 5.7 on 1, 4 and 9). Slide 7's lifted mauve field and slide 3's flat canvas map sit slightly outside the stock.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces. $9.75M, $4.875M and $19.5M trace to c1 and c3, 90, 45 and 135 to c4 plus a sum, 2,393 acres and 42.84 acres to c9 and c10, 2.5M, 2.47M, 2.32M and 11.2M to c17 to c20, and 22 percent is 2,500 over 11,163. The squares on slide 3 measure true: the ranch side is about 294 px against a 152 px mile cell, which is 1.93 mi. 'Mentions AI once' is scoped to the one release, which was read in full (c7). The NASS figures rest on the run's own retrieval after a live 503 and are labelled medium confidence. The release is primary throughout.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: Who (USDA, the A&M System, WT), where (Nance Ranch, seven miles east of Canyon), how much and when ground was broken are all named. The AI stake is the absence of a named tool, which is stated generally, and the close is a question with no body, date or venue a Texan can act on.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook earns the swipe and slide 2 pays the money at once. Slides 3 to 6 are background (ranch, pens, buildings, a state comparison), and 6 could move or go without loss. The turn comes at 7 with the release's own sentence, 8 lands the absence, and 9 closes on the question.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Plain and on register, with Panhandle specifics: the Kuhlman brothers, Nance Ranch, flaked corn in the throat. 'The grant is awarded. The AI approaches are a plan.' is good. Every dek ends on the same 'is drawn to illustrate' tail across nine frames, which reads as machinery.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: This is the third staged lastLight deck in four days. No. 46 (Oct 8th) used lastLight, and no. 48 (Oct 10th) used lastLight with a computed sun at az -77.7 and el 6.4, against today's -79.1 and 6.1. Accent #E0956A repeats no. 43's. The structure repeats too: one chassis object on all nine frames, a squares map, a count frame, a document frame and a kit person at the empty hero on the close, a close that echoes no. 48's empty desk. The feedyard subject and the bunk motif are fresh.

one_sentence_fix: Stop reading kit models at close range and stop shrinking the hero. Re-crop 8 to the ear, tag and eye, recast 9's figure as a posed silhouette against the seam, and re-stage 2 and 4 so the bunk sections and the lit pen triplet each fill a third of the frame, because those four frames are what hold the art at 6.5 while 1 and 5 already show the deck can render at an 8.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Close crop on the primitive kit steer. The hide texture is smeared, the back contour is doubled at about y 680 to 760, the ear flap cuts through the horn and the legs are bare cylinders. The model is biggest exactly where it is weakest.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Move the camera in until only the near ear, the blank tag, the eye and the neck rail fill the frame, and rake that side hard from the west so the face falls into half shadow. The blank tag becomes the subject and the body, legs and back contour leave the frame.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The kit figure stands in a stiff A-pose with plastic hair and flat shirt shading, and the pipe post rises directly out of her cap. It reads as a mannequin at full size.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Swing the camera about 15 degrees toward the bunk so she is backlit against the warm seam as a silhouette, posed with one hand on the top rail and her head turned to the bunk. Move her 0.5 m clear of the post so the post top no longer meets her head.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The bunk sections fill only a thin band from y 1080 to 1340, about an eighth of the frame, between an empty sky above and an empty apron and labels below. The subject doesn't own the frame.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Tighten the long lens from fov 14 to about 8 at the same 26 m so the four sections span the full width and about a third of the frame height. Then re-seat the DOM brackets under the enlarged section joints.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The steers are about 40 px tall, the lamp pools are dim brown smudges that stop short of their fences, and both labels sit on dark plates. Fence lines outweigh the lit pens at 432 px.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Drop the camera from 30 m to about 12 m over the near alley so the one commercial pen and its two small partners fill the lower half. Light each pool out to its fences so those floors are the brightest areas after the type, and set the two labels on the dark field above with the plates removed.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The page hangs before a flat mauve mid-tone backdrop with no true black. The quote's DOM type is axis-aligned while the sheet is skewed, so the words don't sit on the paper, and QA warns of a dead lower zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Take the backdrop behind the rail down to the near-black sky so the page is the one lit thing. Either square the sheet to the camera or transform the quote block to the sheet's skew so the type lies on the paper plane.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The bunk's outer wall is the largest object and the least modelled, a clean pale slab with hairline joints, and the steers' legs read cool lilac from the fill.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Run a grime and splash gradient up the outer wall from its base with wear on the lip, and warm or cut the cool fill so the legs fall to shadow instead of lilac.
